That close button that was removed is the one I used the most in the UI.

I work with hundreds of projects and usually touch 10–20 of them every day.

The left navigation bar with the project list is unusable for me:
- I only see a single letter
- there’s no project name
- the order isn’t sorted in any useful way (MRU would help a lot)

If users might accidentally close a project (which I honestly don’t understand, it’s never happened to me), the solution would be a confirmation prompt, not removing the feature entirely.

### Claude Code's output

  Root Cause: The Drizzle ORM update in commit 5e699c94 (chore(storage): update drizzle and channel db handling) changed migration tracking from hash-based to name-based. The
  __drizzle_migrations table gained a name column, but existing records from older versions don't have entries that the new Drizzle recognizes. So migrate() thinks the initial migration
  (20260127222353_familiar_lady_ursula) was never applied and tries to re-run CREATE TABLE project — which fails because the table already exists.

  Workaround:

```bash
  sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO __drizzle_migrations (hash, created_at, name) SELECT '', 0, v.name FROM (SELECT '20260127222353_familiar_lady_ursula'
   AS name UNION ALL SELECT '20260211171708_add_project_commands' UNION ALL SELECT '20260213144116_wakeful_the_professor' UNION ALL SELECT '20260225215848_workspace' UNION ALL SELECT
  '20260227213759_add_session_workspace_id' UNION ALL SELECT '20260303231226_add_workspace_fields') v WHERE v.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM __drizzle_migrations);"
```

  This backfills the missing migration journal entries so Drizzle knows they were already applied.

  Suggested fix for maintainers: Make migration SQL idempotent at runtime in db.ts by replacing CREATE TABLE → CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and CREATE INDEX → CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS
  before passing entries to migrate(). This would make upgrades resilient to journal corruption or format changes.

Additional data point — grep tool call hanging inside nested subagent (v1.2.21, Linux)

I'm running OpenCode v1.2.21 on Ubuntu 24.04 with a two-layer subagent architecture (primary → subagent → sub-subagent).

A grep tool call inside one of the second-layer subagents hung indefinitely. Because the entire call chain is await-blocked (grep.execute() → child SessionProcessor → parent TaskTool.execute() → primary session loop), the whole session became completely unresponsive — not just the stuck subagent, but every other subagent and the orchestrator itself.

There was no way to cancel only the stuck subagent or the hung tool call. The only escape was killing the entire session (ESC×2).

Root cause insight: Looking at the source, grep (unlike bash) has no timeout at all — it relies entirely on the AbortSignal propagated from SessionPrompt.cancel(). But since there's no per-subagent cancellation in the UI, and no independent watchdog/deadline on tool calls, a single hung ripgrep process cascades into a full session freeze.

What would help (in priority order):

A per-tool-call timeout (e.g., grep should have a configurable timeout like bash already does via OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS)
Per-subagent cancellation — ability to cancel a specific stuck subagent without killing the entire session
A global subagent deadline configurable in opencode.json (e.g., "timeout": 300 per agent definition)

> **Additional finding: streaming mode hides the actual error message**
> 
> Reproduced this on `claude-opus-4-6` via OpenCode v1.2.22 web (also affects TUI when the model responds with text-only, i.e. `finish="stop"`).
> 
> **Key detail for anyone debugging via a custom gateway/proxy**: When `stream: true` is set (OpenCode's default), the Anthropic API returns a **400 with an empty body** (`content-length: 0`). This completely hides the actual error:
> 
> ```
> "This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message."
> ```
> 
> You only get the real error when replaying the request with `"stream": false`. This also means any error-recovery middleware (like oh-my-opencode's `session-recovery` hook) that pattern-matches on the error text **cannot detect or recover from this failure**.
> 
> **Reproduction**: any new web session → send a simple message like "Hello" → model responds with text (`finish="stop"`) → next request includes assistant prefill with `cache_control` → 400.
> 
> TUI appears unaffected in practice because the model typically responds with tool calls (`finish="tool-calls"`), which skips the prefill code path.

I did see same error with TUI as well, with #14772, the issue has been gone for me, but TBH I am not 100% sure if it fixes the root.

## Update: Consolidated fixes from 23+ community PRs

I've reviewed every open memory leak PR referenced in #16697 and consolidated the best version of each fix into this branch. The latest commit (`b395d19`) adds **17 more files** on top of the original 15, bringing the total to **30 files changed**.

### New fixes added (from community PRs)

| Fix | Source PRs | Impact |
|-----|-----------|--------|
| **Plugin subscriber stacking** — `Bus.subscribeAll()` unsub before re-init | #16346, #7914 | Prevents permanent wildcard listener accumulation |
| **Subagent deallocation** — `Session.remove()` after task completion | #14650 | GB-scale savings in long sessions with many subagents |
| **SSE stream cleanup** — centralized `cleanup()` + `done` guard on 3 endpoints | #15646 | Prevents leaked handlers/intervals on ungraceful disconnect |
| **Compaction data trimming** — clear `output` and `attachments` on prune | #14650, #7049 | Frees 200KB+ per compacted tool call |
| **Process exit cleanup** — `Instance.disposeAll()` with 5s timeout in finally block | #13186, #15646 | Prevents zombie LSP/MCP/PTY processes |
| **Serve command** — graceful shutdown instead of `await new Promise(() => {})` | #13186 | Fixes unreachable cleanup code in serve mode |
| **Bash tool ring buffer** — chunks array with 10MB cap instead of `output += chunk` | #13186, #7914 | Eliminates O(n²) string growth for long commands |
| **LSP index teardown** — clear `clients`/`broken`/`spawning` on dispose | #16346 | Prevents stale client references after teardown |
| **LSP open-files cap** — evict oldest when >1000 tracked files | #14650 | Prevents unbounded `files` object growth |
| **Format subscription cleanup** — store and cleanup unsub handle on re-init | #10392, #7914 | Prevents listener stacking |
| **Permission `clearSession()`** — reject pending promises on session delete | #14650, #10392 | Prevents leaked promises holding closures |
| **Question `clearSession()`** — reject pending promises on session delete | #10392, #13186 | Same as above |
| **Session.remove() cleanup chain** — calls FileTime, Permission, Question cleanup | #10392 | Per-session state freed on deletion |
| **ShareNext subscription cleanup** — store unsub handles, cleanup on dispose/re-init | #10392, #7914 | Prevents 4 Bus listeners stacking per init cycle |
| **OAuth transport close** — close existing transport before replacing | #9145 | Prevents abandoned HTTP transports accumulating |

### What's NOT in this PR (and why)

Some fixes from the community PRs were intentionally excluded:

- **`Bun.gc()` calls** (#16346, #13186) — forcing GC is a band-aid; the actual leaks are fixed instead
- **Diagnostics/monitoring module** (#15646) — good idea but out of scope for a leak fix PR
- **Instance idle-timeout with ref counting** (#16616) — valuable but architecturally significant; should be its own PR
- **LSP stderr `"ignore"`** (#16241) — changes 40+ spawn sites across server definitions; better as a targeted PR
- **LRU cache utility + provider cache bounds** (#10392, #9149) — new abstraction layer; merits separate review
- **ACP session manager TTL/eviction** (#12259, #9146) — requires design decision on TTL values
- **Startup cleanup/maintenance system** (#16628) — new feature (config schema, vacuum, retention); should be separate
- **AsyncQueue close()** (#13594) — API change to a shared utility; needs its own review
- **O(n²) string concat in processor.ts** (#13186, #10392) — the throttled flush approach is complex; needs careful review to avoid breaking streaming UX
- **SDK SSE buffer cap / abort listener `{ once: true }`** (#14650) — changes are in `packages/sdk/`, not `packages/opencode/`; separate package, separate PR

### Verification

- `tsgo --noEmit` passes cleanly across all 19 packages
- Pre-commit typecheck hook passed on push

## Consolidated fix PR: #16695

I reviewed every one of the 23+ open PRs listed in this issue, analyzed the diffs, identified overlapping fixes, and consolidated the best version of each into a single PR: **#16695** (branch `fix/memory-leaks`).

### Coverage: 30 files, 3 commits

The PR addresses the following categories from the issue table:

| Category | Status | Details |
|----------|--------|---------|
| TUI event listeners | ✅ Fixed | `onCleanup` for all `sdk.event.on()` calls in app.tsx, prompt, session route |
| Unbounded Maps/Sets | ✅ Fixed | Bus/RPC empty entry deletion, diagnostics LRU cap (200), open-files cap (1000), LSP index teardown |
| Timer/interval leaks | ✅ Fixed | Leader timeout, models refresh, state disposal timeout, theme SIGUSR2 |
| Session data retention | ✅ Fixed | Sync store frees previous session data, `clearSession()` on Permission/Question/FileTime |
| Plugin subscriber stacking | ✅ Fixed | `unsub?.()` before re-subscribing in `Plugin.init()` |
| Message array retention | ✅ Fixed | Event queue capped at 1000 |
| Subagent deallocation | ✅ Fixed | `Session.remove()` after task tool completion |
| SSE stream leaks | ✅ Fixed | Centralized `cleanup()` with `done` guard on all 3 SSE endpoints |
| Process/Bus cleanup | ✅ Fixed | `Instance.disposeAll()` with 5s timeout on exit, serve cmd graceful shutdown |
| Subscription disposal | ✅ Fixed | Format, ShareNext, Plugin all store and cleanup unsub handles |
| Tool output retention | ✅ Fixed | `output = ""`, `attachments = undefined` on compaction prune |
| OAuth transport leaks | ✅ Fixed | Close existing transport before replacing |
| Bash tool output | ✅ Fixed | Chunks array with 10MB ring buffer instead of O(n²) `+=` |

### Items left for follow-up PRs

These are valuable but architecturally significant enough to warrant separate review:

- **Instance idle-timeout disposal** (serve mode ref counting) — #16616
- **LSP stderr `"ignore"`** (40+ spawn site changes) — #16241
- **Provider/SDK LRU caches** (new cache abstraction) — #10392, #9149
- **ACP session TTL/eviction** — #12259, #9146
- **Startup cleanup/maintenance system** (config schema, vacuum) — #16628
- **O(n²) string concat in processor.ts** (throttled flush) — #13186
- **Database config** (auto_vacuum, WAL checkpoint, retention) — #16730
- **SDK-level fixes** (SSE buffer cap, abort `{ once: true }`) — #14650

The goal was to ship the highest-impact, lowest-risk fixes in one shot. The remaining items are individually reviewable without blocking on this PR.

Greptile Summary

This PR replaces Bun's native HTTP/WebSocket runtime (`Bun.serve` + `hono/bun`) with the portable `@hono/node-server` and `@hono/node-ws` adapters, making the opencode server runtime-agnostic. The key architectural changes are: (1) `Server.listen` is now `async` and returns a typed `Listener` abstraction instead of a raw `Bun.Server`; (2) `PtyRoutes` is converted from a lazy singleton to a factory that accepts the `UpgradeWebSocket` function, injected at app-construction time; (3) a `key()` helper is extracted in `Pty` to normalise the subscriber identity across both Bun's data-carrying sockets and plain node WebSockets; and (4) all CLI entrypoints properly `await` start and stop. - The overall refactoring is clean and well-scoped. All callers correctly `await` the new async `listen()`. - The subscriber `key()` helper in `pty/index.ts` is the right approach for cross-adapter identity, though renaming the for-loop iterator from `key` to `id` in the same commit introduces shadowing of the outer PTY session ID variable in `create()` and `remove()`. - `server.stop()` calls `closeAllConnections()` followed by `closeIdleConnections()` — the second call is redundant since the first already drains all connections. - When `opts.port === 0` triggers a port-4096 → port-0 retry, `built.ws.injectWebSocket` is called on the abandoned first server before the fallback. This is harmless in practice but slightly surprising. - The previously exported `Server.createApp` function has been removed (replaced by private `create`); no usages exist in the monorepo, so this is not a breaking change.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge — no critical logic errors; the identified issues are style/quality concerns that do not affect correctness. - The migration is mechanically straightforward and all callers are updated consistently. The three flagged issues (loop-variable shadowing, redundant closeIdleConnections, and double injectWebSocket on retry) are all non-breaking style or robustness concerns rather than functional bugs. - packages/opencode/src/pty/index.ts (variable shadowing) and packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts (stop() cleanup ordering, port-retry injection)

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts | Core change — replaces Bun.serve/websocket with createAdaptorServer + createNodeWebSocket; exposes a clean Listener type with async start/stop; minor issues with redundant closeIdleConnections and double injectWebSocket on port retry. | | packages/opencode/src/pty/index.ts | Refactors subscriber key logic into a shared `key()` helper; renames loop iterator from `key` to `id`, inadvertently shadowing outer PTY session ID in `create()` and `remove()` — functionally correct today but fragile. | | packages/opencode/src/server/routes/pty.ts | Converts PtyRoutes from a lazy singleton to a factory function that accepts an UpgradeWebSocket injector, cleanly decoupling it from the Bun-specific import. | | packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/worker.ts | Removes the Bun-typed server variable, replaces it with the new Listener type, and properly awaits both server.listen and server.stop(true) on shutdown. |

## History of the Modified Code

### Timeline

| Date | Commit | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| **2025-11-28** | `13f89fdb8` (PR #4811) | **First empty-message filter** added in `message-v2.ts`. A community contributor (DS / @Tarquinen) added `.filter((msg) => msg.parts.length > 0)` before `convertToModelMessages()` to prevent crashing when empty messages hit the AI SDK. Only filtered at the UIMessage level — no part-level filtering. |
| **2026-01-05** | `c285304a` (no PR, direct commit) | **Anthropic empty-content filter** added in `transform.ts` by Aiden Cline. Anthropic's API rejects messages with empty content, so this filters out empty `text` **and** `reasoning` parts from array content, and removes messages that become empty. Applied to **all roles** (user, assistant, tool) indiscriminately. Tests all used `role: "assistant"` messages. |
| **2026-01-20** | `021e42c0b` (no PR, direct commit) | **`differentModel` guard** added in `message-v2.ts` by Aiden Cline. When switching between providers, stale `providerMetadata` (e.g. Anthropic signatures sent to OpenAI) caused 400 errors. Fix: only include `providerMetadata` when the model matches. This introduced the conditional `...(differentModel ? {} : { providerMetadata: part.metadata })`. |
| **2026-02-13** | `0d90a22f9` (PR #13439) | **Opus 4.6 adaptive thinking** enabled on vertex/bedrock/anthropic. This is when Opus 4.6 started producing interleaved reasoning blocks with cryptographic signatures, creating the conditions for the bug. |

### How the bug emerged

The empty-content filter from Jan 5 (`c285304a`) was written **before** Opus 4.6 adaptive thinking existed (Feb 13). At the time, reasoning parts with empty text were genuinely useless — there were no cryptographic signatures to preserve. The filter treated all roles identically.

Once Opus 4.6 arrived, it began producing patterns like:

```
reasoning(sig1) → text("") → reasoning(sig2) → text("answer")
```

The empty `text("")` is structurally significant — the signatures encode positional context. There are **two independent stripping points**:

1. **`transform.ts`**: The `normalizeMessages` filter removes `text("")` from assistant messages, shifting the reasoning block positions and invalidating signatures.

2. **`message-v2.ts`**: Even if `transform.ts` is fixed, the AI SDK's internal `convertToLanguageModelPrompt` strips text parts where `text === "" && providerOptions == null`. The `differentModel` guard from Jan 20 was correct for its purpose (don't send foreign metadata), but when `part.metadata` is `undefined` for an empty text part from the same model, the resulting `providerMetadata: undefined` causes the AI SDK to strip the part.

### PRs in flight

- **PR #16750** (this branch's upstream PR, opened 2026-03-09): The fix under review. Skips empty-text filtering for assistant messages with reasoning blocks in `transform.ts`, and adds the `providerMetadata: {}` fallback in `message-v2.ts`.

- **PR #14393** (opened 2026-02-20, still open): An earlier, broader attempt at fixing the signature stripping problem that proposed **removing the `differentModel` guard entirely** (always pass metadata through). That PR also bundled a compaction headroom fix. It was never merged — presumably because always passing foreign provider metadata was considered too risky. The current branch's approach is more surgical: keep the guard but patch the specific empty-text-with-no-metadata case.

### Summary

The code being modified was never designed for the Opus 4.6 world. The empty-content filter (`c285304a`, Jan 5) predates adaptive thinking by 5+ weeks and assumed empty parts are always safe to strip. The `differentModel` metadata guard (`021e42c0b`, Jan 20) was solving a real cross-provider problem but created a gap where same-model empty text parts lose their metadata lifeline. Both pieces of code were correct when written — the bug is an emergent interaction with Opus 4.6's signature-sensitive thinking blocks.
